title: Hubble spies NGC 3274
caption: The spiral galaxy NGC 3274, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 3274 · constellation Leo · about 20 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image shows NGC 3274, a relatively faint spiral galaxy in Leo, more than 20 million light-years from Earth. In the upper right is another galaxy, PGC 213714, which lies much farther from Earth.

The picture was made with Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, which can see from ultraviolet light through to the near infrared. That range lets astronomers study many kinds of targets, from star formation nearby to galaxies in the most remote parts of the cosmos. For this image, observations through five different filters were combined, bringing ultraviolet, visible and infrared light together in one view.

Like all Hubble data, the image benefits from the telescope's position above Earth's atmosphere, which would otherwise blur the view. From orbit, the camera can return sharp, detailed images again and again.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.64 x 2.30 arcminutes) and distance (20 million light years), the frame spans roughly 15,000 × 13,000 light-years. Its light set out about 20 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, combining five filters from 275 to 814 nm, spanning ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared light. The colours assigned to each filter are not published.
understand.eye: Ultraviolet and near-infrared light are invisible to the eye, and a galaxy this faint cannot be seen in such detail without a space telescope.

behind.people: See full credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, D. Calzetti

behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: NGC 3274 was discovered in 1783 by Wilhelm Herschel. Much later, Hubble's cameras can study it in light that Herschel could never have seen, including ultraviolet and near-infrared wavelengths, and with far sharper detail.
alt: A faint spiral galaxy, with a smaller, more distant galaxy in the upper right.
